title: Dedicated Webinar Tool or Unified Platform? Zuddl vs. Goldcast, ON24 and GoToWebinar | Zuddl Blog
summary: Want to consolidate your webinar stack? See when an event platform like Zuddl can replace Goldcast, ON24 or GoTo Webinar, and when a dedicated tool still wins.
body_markdown:
It's not easy evaluating webinar platforms for a few reasons. One, you probably already pay for a point solution that does webinars well. Two, you're not sure if a unified platform is a true value-add or not.


The way comparison content is normally written doesn't help either. You know that one tool will be subtly advocated for, or maybe you get a feature checklist which says nothing about how tools would fit into your workflow.


This page compares Zuddl against Goldcast, ON24, GoToWebinar, Livestorm, and BigMarker on the features that event teams would use to evaluate if a switch makes sense: registration and branding depth, CRM integration, analytics, and total cost.


We've based our assessment about when Zuddl replaces a dedicated webinar tool and when it does not on our own calls with prospects and customers. We've also added a framework for calculating what switching tools costs you.


## What does consolidating your event and webinar stack actually change?


Collapsing a multi-tool stack into one platform removes the stitching and re-syncing between disconnected tools, and puts webinar and event data in a single attendee record that feeds into the CRM. Marketing, sales and ops can all pull from that data, and see which webinars influenced pipeline.


### Fewer tools to maintain and pay for


‍


Most teams stitch together a webinar platform, their marketing automation tool for registration forms and invites, and web-team-built landing pages, then export all that data to reconcile and report on it.


Each handoff means either paying for a pre-built integration, or building and maintaining a solution yourself. This can add up pretty quick:[organizations running five to eight tools in their event stack can spend $25,000 to $100,000 on integration work alone](https://web.snapsight.com/glossary/event-technology-stack/) . Zuddl takes over the webinar platform and the landing pages, and syncs with the marketing automation tool you already use.


### A complete attendee record without manual reconciliation


When you're working across multiple tools, each one only has data to understand a slice of what happened at an event. Without manual reconciliation, you can't see the full picture of how an attendee behaved across the event (like the sessions they attended, what their survey answers were, or which polls they engaged with). This makes pipeline attribution and program-level reporting harder to produce.


‍


On a unified platform like Zuddl, all dashboards pull from a connected dataset with real-time synced data between your CRM, your marketing automation tool, and the platform that builds a record of your attendee across all your events. For example, sales can see which accounts voted in a specific way before they start outreach.[A unified data layer means sales, ops and event teams work from the same baseline.](https://www.eventcombo.com/a/unified-event-platform-for-event-data-management)


### The operational gain is marketer self-sufficiency


With a unified platform,[a single B2B marketer can run the entire webinar production process without extensive design or dev involvement](https://www.zuddl.com/blog/how-zuddls-webinar-platform-enables-a-1-person-team-to-run-webinars) . This is because the registration, landing page, communications, studio and analytics all sit in the same tool, and each is no-code. That matters when a team is running webinars, field events and a conference in the same quarter, and every request to IT or design means extra days to launch.


[Bandwidth cut webinar setup time by 50% after moving to Zuddl](https://www.zuddl.com/customer-stories/how-bandwidth-cut-webinar-setup-time-by-50-and-drove-higher-engagement-with-zuddl) . Before Zuddl, preparing a webinar meant multiple test calls with speakers and weeks of setup, and live engagement was hard to measure. Its STIR/SHAKEN updates webinar launched in three weeks instead of six to eight, with attendees staying longer and interacting more. Their sales, product and legal teams can now launch on-brand webinar programs independently.


## Can Zuddl replace Goldcast, ON24 or GoToWebinar? A feature checklist


A marketing ops practitioner recently called Zuddl "essentially a Goldcast replacement."


Zuddl is a viable replacement for Goldcast, ON24 or GoToWebinar because you get registration, landing pages, the live studio, engagement tools, analytics and CRM sync in one platform. The work of exporting data or moving it between tools is completely eliminated.


It becomes even more useful if you run more than webinars. You get fully customizable brand kits built from a reference URL, unified event data across formats, bi-directional CRM sync, and more features that help you run a scalable event program.


Roughly 9 in 10 teams that use Zuddl run more than webinars on the platform, and about half run webinars alongside in-person or virtual events.


That said, for a webinar-only program with simple needs, the fit question is more nuanced and covered in the section below.

### Where are other platforms the strongest when it comes to webinars?


Goldcast has built its product around content repurposing: its editing tools and content distribution workflow are purpose-built for that use case. If turning webinar recordings into clips, blog posts and social assets is the primary job, Goldcast works well.


However, teams using Goldcast often build registration pages on their own site or in their marketing automation tool and pass registrations to Goldcast. Some teams raise doubts about live reliability across multiple concurrent events, and smaller gaps include an attendee cap on networking and an awkward series setup with HubSpot forms. Users also report that the Marketo integration isn't flexible enough, and that the newer field events product has gaps for in-person programs.


ON24 puts attendee-level engagement data and scoring at the center, pushed into Salesforce, Marketo, HubSpot and Eloqua, alongside content hubs for post-event nurture.


If scoring depth or simulive is the main requirement, ON24 is worth a look. The trade-off is that it's expensive to use and teams tell us the setup effort is high. Teams find it dated and too heavy for smaller programs that only need simple webinars. Users also report limited recording export options and date-range limits on reports.


GoToWebinar works well for teams running low-frequency, low-complexity webinars. At that scale and budget, the simpler tool is usually the right one. You have to do manual work to export poll, hand-raiser and attendee data, and deal with weaker video quality with blurred or custom backgrounds, attendee caps per event. In its favor, it is inexpensive, it has iOS and Android apps for attendees, it supports simulive webinars, and its Marketo connection is easy to set up.


### Where Zuddl goes beyond just a webinar replacement


Most event teams don't run webinars in isolation. The same person might attend a webinar, visit your booth at a trade show and come to a field dinner, and if you have a different tool to handle each event format, those touchpoints are hard to connect across the program.


Event teams might be running webinars on Zoom, registration and ticketing through another platform, in-person events on a conference tool, and lead capture on a third-party scanner.


‍


Zuddl runs conferences, field events, webinars and third-party events (including lead capture) on one codebase inside one tool. That means attendee data from every format flows into the same analytics and CRM sync, without manual exports between tools.


For teams whose switching trigger is CRM integration failure or analytics that cannot show pipeline influence across event types, that is the structural difference.


In practice, that looks like:


- **One workspace for webinars and field events:** A company that previously ran webinars on BigMarker and field events on Splash now builds both in their Zuddl workspace, with a webinar event type for virtual sessions and a separate in-person event type with badge scanning. Its Marketo and Salesforce data now syncs from one source.
- **Live attendance data from field dinners:** A team hosting customer dinners used to reconcile attendance after each event by uploading check-in lists to Salesforce. Now guests are scanned in at the door and their status appears in the campaign live.
- **More leads captured at trade show booths:** A team that typed booth conversations in by hand switched to Zuddl lead capture at third-party conferences and saw "a lot more leads come in" than with manual entry. The same team uses Zuddl for onsite registration, badge printing and event landing pages.


## How do Zuddl's webinar features work and what do they replace?


Zuddl covers the core webinar feature set — registration and landing pages, branding and custom environments, polls, Q&A, martech and CRM integrations, analytics, and on-demand hosting — from a single interface. Each of these features takes the place of a separate tool that most teams run today, allowing webinar data to stay in one system instead of being exported and matched to CRM records manually.


### Registration and landing pages


[Zuddl's landing page builder](https://www.zuddl.com/platform/event-registration-and-ticketing-software/landing-page-builder) lets teams build fully branded, customizable event and webinar pages without developer involvement, replacing standalone page-builder tools. The registration flow builder is part of the tool as well and gives you[multi-step, conditional registration flows](https://support.zuddl.com/articles/8970287803-registration-flow-introduction) with custom CSS branding.


‍


The same flow builder is available for conferences and field events as well. Widgets for schedule, speakers and sponsors can be built within Zuddl across event formats, so you don't need a separate tool to manage each page element.


Exit Five used Zuddl to[build pages in a day and a half](https://www.zuddl.com/customer-stories/sold-out-in-a-day-how-zuddl-powered-exit-fives-drive) without going back and forth with developers.


> Danielle Messler, Head of Content at Exit Five, said: "I'm a perfectionist. It saved me so much time and stress."


### Branding and custom environments


Most webinar platforms force teams into generic templates, which prevents teams from standardizing their branding in line with the rest of their marketing. Zuddl lets teams build a[brand kit from a reference URL](https://www.zuddl.com/agentic-events-platform) and use custom overlays and scenes in the live studio, with no-code landing pages and registration flows, so webinars match the company's overall brand without developer involvement.


‍


Teams comparing Zuddl against cheaper point solutions value the ability to control the full visual environment for their webinars, not just a logo and a color, is a huge reason why teams that want brand consistency in their programs choose a unified platform like Zuddl over a point solution.


### Polls, Q&A and engagement


‍


Zuddl includes embedded polls, Q&A, live chat, emoji reactions, resources and embedded CTAs inside the webinar environment. Because engagement is a part of the same platform as registration, each poll answer, question and CTA click is stored on the attendee's record and can sync to your CRM or marketing automation platform.


### Martech and CRM integrations


Zuddl's native integrations cover Salesforce, HubSpot, Marketo, Eloqua, Pardot and more. Registration status, attendance, no-show flags and session engagement (poll answers, questions, CTA clicks and time in session) write back to the CRM record without a manual export step, and connected fields can pull CRM data back into Zuddl.


Status mapping covers invited, pending, registered, attended, engaged and no-show states, along with trackable activity types, which is the data a sales team needs to act on a webinar lead the same day.[Every sync is logged with its status](https://www.zuddl.com/blog/smarter-coupons-integration-logs-shareable-reports) , so if a record fails to reach the CRM, the team can see which one and retry it.


### On-demand and evergreen webinars


After a live session, the recording can go straight to on-demand on the same event, gated behind the registration form to capture new leads, or ungated for open access.


‍


Replay views are tracked on each attendee's record, so you get on-demand engagement in the CRM as well. Highlights from the session can be edited and downloaded, and the full recording can be pushed directly to Wistia or Vimeo. That removes the usual download-and-reupload loop between the webinar tool and a separate video host.


## Is an event platform worth it if you only run webinars?


For a team running webinars exclusively at low frequency, with no need for custom branded environments or cross-event data, a dedicated tool is the more practical choice. An event platform like Zuddl is built for programs that span multiple event types and need unified data across all of them.


### When a dedicated tool is the better fit


[A team that runs only one or two virtual events a year pays for capacity it does not use](https://theknowledgeengineers.com/software-advice/virtual-event-platform) . If the program has no roadmap beyond recurring webinars, no requirement to connect webinar data to field or conference data, and no need for a custom-branded environment, a lighter tool will cost less and require less onboarding time.


The[on-demand webinar platforms roundup](https://www.zuddl.com/blog/13-best-on-demand-webinar-platforms-for-b2b-event-teams) evaluates 13 platforms across broadcast mode flexibility, CRM sync depth, and content repurposing capability, which helps if you want to compare lighter options before deciding.


### When the platform cost justifies itself


The calculus shifts when the program is growing beyond webinars or the data layer matters.[Teams whose programs have outgrown point solutions and need branded production, bi-directional CRM sync, and consolidated analytics across event types](https://www.zuddl.com/blog/best-virtual-event-platforms-large-scale-attendee-experiences) are where a unified platform earns its cost. Running separate tools for different event types forces data into separate systems, which makes it harder to create a consistent experience for audiences as well as making program-level reporting difficult.


CreatorIQ runs its webinar series, quarterly roadshows, 1,000-person flagship events in London and Los Angeles, and trade-show lead capture on Zuddl, after moving off Eventbrite and Splash. With landing pages, check-in, badge printing and lead capture in one system and lead data flowing into Salesforce, the team saves[10–12 hours of manual work per event,](https://www.zuddl.com/customer-stories/how-creatoriq-cut-check-in-time-by-35-and-boosted-attendance-by-12) and webinar registrations rose 10%.


### What should you check before you decide?


‍


Before committing to either path, consider these four factors:


- Annual webinar volume: fewer than 12 per year (less than one a month), with no other event types, usually means a point solution tool is better, because at that scale you can manage repeat setups or manual data reconciliation
- Event types: any field events, conferences or hybrid events on the roadmap shift the balance toward a unified platform
- Custom environments: if you need full control over the brand and the attendee experience, a unified platform is better
- Martech integration depth: a team that needs bi-directional CRM sync, automated Salesforce child campaign mapping, or session-level engagement data routed to their MAP will find a dedicated tool's integration limited


## What triggers a platform switch, and how do you know you have outgrown your current webinar tool?


When your roadmap includes in-person or hybrid events and your webinar tool cannot handle them, or when you are maintaining three or more separate tools to run a single event, there is a gap between what your program requires and what your tool can support.


### Trigger 1: data fragmentation after every event


After a webinar, you export registrants and attendees from the webinar tool, pull poll answers from a second report, and match both against CRM records so sales can follow up. A few of those contacts were checked in at your field dinner last week, and adding that context is down to you .


Running separate tools creates these data silos. Until someone reconciles them by hand, sales can't act on what happened at the webinar, and by the time the data is clean, the follow-up window has passed.


Teams typically evaluate a switch when engagement data does not integrate cleanly with CRM systems and analytics fail to demonstrate pipeline influence. Manual reconciliation is a clear sign that your tools were not designed to work together.


### Trigger 2: branding that stops at the template


Brand control comes up regularly when teams evaluate a switch. Event teams we speak with are looking for a tool that doesn't lack any customization options, where they don't have to route every landing page through the web dev team because their webinar tool couldn't produce on-brand pages.


That means full control over the visual environment, from the landing page and registration flow to the confirmation and reminder emails and the overlays and scenes on the live stream.


If your current tool only gives you pre-built templates or minimal customization, the brand work you do everywhere else doesn't reflect in your webinars unless you spend a lot of time with the web dev team to customize every asset.


### Trigger 3: a program that has grown past webinars


A webinar tool is built for webinars. When you're also running field events, a user conference or trade shows, you add other tools for registration, check-in and lead capture. You might have contracts renewing at different times for different parts of the same program, with attendee data split between them.


Exit Five ran live sessions, virtual events and ticketed in-person meetups across a patchwork of tools that was "expensive, inconsistent, and downright frustrating," going back and forth with developers to get landing pages built.


Their COO Dan Murphy said this about Zuddl, "With Zuddl, we centralize everything — virtual, in-person, and webinars — in one place. It minimizes risk and creates a consistent experience for our audience."


### How to use these triggers to shortlist


Apply the triggers to your current situation before comparing platforms:


- **Data fragmentation:** keep only platforms that sync poll answers, questions and attendance to the contact record in your CRM, not just registrations, and that show you when a sync fails. Ask to test the integration against your own CRM sandbox.
- **Branding limits:** keep only platforms where your team can build a fully branded event page, registration flow and reminder emails without a developer. Test it by building one with your own brand assets.
- **Program expansion:** keep only platforms that run the event types on your next year's roadmap natively, such as in-person check-in, lead capture or conferences, rather than through a third-party integration.


## How do you compare the total cost of switching webinar platforms?


Compare the full stack cost beyond the license line item. That means adding up the base cost of the tool with every add-on you have to purchase/build, and the time spent keeping integrations working.


‍


### Step 1: List every tool in your current stack


Start with your webinar platform license, then work outward. The tools that sit alongside a webinar platform to fill gaps it does not cover — dedicated registration funnels, CRM middleware, email and SMS sequencing, and analytics overlays — can add $150 to $1000 a month to what a team actually spends.


### Step 2: Estimate integration maintenance time


Once you have the list, attach a time cost to each connection. Organizations running five to eight tools in their event stack can spend $25,000 to $100,000 on integration work often more than the individual tools cost.


‍


For each integration your team maintains, estimate the hours per month spent on mapping, debugging, and re-syncing data, then convert that to a fully-loaded cost: multiply the hours by the hourly rate of whoever does the work (annual salary plus benefits and overhead, divided by working hours).


### Step 3: Factor in your event needs beyond webinars


Start with your audience and your plans.


**If your company already runs other formats** , whether through your team or another one like field marketing or sales: check how many webinar attendees also show up at those events, and which tools those events run on.


**If you only run webinars today** , ask two questions about the next 12–24 months:


- Do you plan to add a conference, roadshow or field series, or is leadership asking for one?
- Are sales or attendees asking for face-to-face time?


**Then decide.** If the answers to both the questions above is no, a dedicated webinar tool may be the right fit for now.


### Step 4: Budget for the migration window


Most teams don't flip a switch. Plan for an overlap of a month or two, with one month to set up and one month running both, so the team can build templates, train up and run a first event before the old contract ends.


If budget is tight, time the decision so the overlap falls in the last months of the old contract rather than paying for an extension.


### What to ask vendors before you sign


Bring this framework into every vendor conversation. Ask specifically for:


- Named integration support: which CRM and MAP connections are native and maintained by the vendor
- Migration assistance: whether the vendor assigns a migration resource or leaves your team to move data alone
- Contract flexibility: whether the term allows an overlap period without penalty


If you're replacing several tools, moving to a unified platform is a change of category, not a like-for-like swap. Compare it against the combined cost of everything it replaces: each license, its integrations, and the manual work between them. If you're only replacing a webinar tool, a direct price comparison is fair, so check what's included at each tier rather than assuming the broader platform costs more


## How do you migrate webinars from your current platform?


Most of a migration is rebuilding, not moving data. Your history stays in your CRM. What you move is your recordings, your templates and your upcoming registrants.


‍


### Step 1: Archive recordings, then re-publish the ones you still promote


Download every recording, deck and resource to a shared drive before your license ends. Then upload the recordings you still use as[on-demand content](https://support.zuddl.com/articles/7187032415-how-to-publish-webinar-recordings-on-demand) on the new platform. In Zuddl, a past Zoom recording can be[uploaded](https://support.zuddl.com/articles/4377919897-how-to-manage-studio-recordings) and published on demand directly.


### Step 2: Leave attendance history in your CRM


Past registrations, attendance and engagement already live on your CRM and marketing automation records. Don't try to re-create them as events on the new platform. Import only upcoming registrants and invite lists, by[CSV](https://support.zuddl.com/articles/2616270622-how-to-add-attendees-to-a-zuddl-webinar-using-csv-import) or through a[CRM workflow](https://support.zuddl.com/articles/4254139667-receive-registrations-from-hubspot-to-zuddl) .


### Step 3: Rebuild your templates first


Landing pages, registration flows, emails and brand themes are where the hours go. Rebuild your most-used formats as[templates](https://support.zuddl.com/articles/1990004738-how-to-duplicate-a-webinar-in-zuddl) before scheduling anything new, or ask the vendor whether migration services can do it for you.


### Step 4: Reconnect integrations and test end to end


[Map fields](https://support.zuddl.com/articles/6271221163-send-registrations-from-zuddl-to-salesforce) with marketing ops, then run a test registration and a short test session and confirm that status and engagement reach the CRM record before your first live webinar.


### Step 5: Run one live event during the overlap


Schedule your first live webinar on the new platform while the old contract is still active.


## Frequently asked questions


**Can Zuddl replace a dedicated webinar tool like Goldcast or ON24?**


For many B2B marketing teams, yes. A marketing ops professional evaluating the switch described Zuddl as being "essentially Goldcast replacement." for their webinar program. Zuddl covers registration, branded production, engagement tools, CRM sync, and on-demand content from one platform. The practical question is whether your program also runs field events or conferences: if it does, a unified platform removes the need for separate tools entirely.[Goldcast has gaps in its hybrid event support and no mobile app](https://www.zuddl.com/compare/goldcast) .


**Is an event platform worth it if you only run webinars?**


It depends on volume and trajectory. Teams that run webinars at scale, need branded production, and want bi-directional CRM sync without stitching separate tools together benefit from consolidation even on a webinar-only program. In Forrester's Q1 2026 State Of B2B Events Survey,[62% of organizations with a deep integration between their event platform and their sales and marketing stack were satisfied with event performance](https://www.forrester.com/blogs/the-next-era-of-b2b-events-eight-data-backed-shifts-defining-2026/) , against 37% of those that had not integrated.


**What is the best webinar platform for B2B marketing teams in 2026?**


There is no single answer, because the right fit depends on what you are optimizing for. Zuddl, Goldcast, and ON24 are[among the platforms most commonly evaluated by B2B marketing teams](https://www.zuddl.com/blog/best-virtual-event-platforms-large-scale-attendee-experiences) , each built around a different priority: multi-format event support across webinars, field events, and conferences (Zuddl); content repurposing and video-first programs (Goldcast); or high-volume structured webinar programs (ON24). Match the platform to your programs primary constraint, not to a ranked list.


**How long does it take to migrate webinars from one platform to another?**


Budget a 30 to 60 day parallel-run window where both platforms are active simultaneously, because an extra month of the outgoing license is cheaper than data loss mid-migration. The migration work itself covers historical recordings, registration data, CRM field mappings, and email templates. Teams that have built complex automation sequences on the outgoing platform should map those flows before they touch the new one.


**Which webinar platform is best for small businesses with a limited budget?**


Zuddl is not the right fit for a low-frequency, budget-constrained team. Zuddl rewards volume and is built for programs that have outgrown point solutions. For small teams running infrequent webinars, a lighter dedicated tool is the more practical starting point.
